structured_output.analysis: The best grid, iso_3.15, measures KL=0.43614 [E514ab09c524e] at avg_bits=3.14795. The budget is 403/128 = 3.14844 bits, which leaves about 0.0005 bits/weight of headroom. That is far too little to pay for any int2→int3 or int3→int4 upgrade on a 3.1M-parameter MLP layer, since each costs about 1 bit/weight on that layer. Every loss-concentration layer already uses its lowest-KL method at its bit width: 27.up gptq_int3 0.00572 vs rht 0.00774 [Ef04d8aa7bded, E8972491007e7]; 3.up rht_gptq_int3 0.00642 vs gptq 0.00706 [E6f4f7ea296d5, Ec98ddfd45576]; 2.up gptq_int3 0.00642 vs rht 0.00656 [E9baa10763ebe, E443dcc5e2e34]; 1.up rht_gptq_int3 0.00611 [E0564bc6ad1eb]; 27.gate rht_gptq_int3 0.00499 [Efa0bb391da67]. Swapping to a different method at the same width therefore gives nothing. The only downgrades that could fund an upgrade would cost about 0.02 KL each (int3→int2), more than the 0.0035–0.0045 an upgrade gains, e.g. 14.down rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 → rht_gptq_int3 0.00181 [E4c3f9b73e065, E90bd4b2f3645]. So this round tests GPTQ option changes that do not change the bit count: activation ordering, and act_order plus a smaller damping value. These target the high activation-kurtosis layers, e.g. 27.up activation kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Turns on act_order=true for all GPTQ-family methods and leaves the grid and stored bits unchanged (avg_bits=3.14795, KL=0.43614 [E514ab09c524e]). The worst layers sit behind heavy-tailed activations: 27.up activation kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a] with gptq_int3 KL 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded], and 3.up activation kurtosis 241.283 [Eb1b68d163774] with rht_gptq_int3 KL 0.00642 [E6f4f7ea296d5]. Quantizing high-activation columns first should cut the GPTQ error on these layers.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: Same grid and bits as iso_3.15 (KL=0.43614 [E514ab09c524e]), with act_order=true and damp=0.005 in place of the default 0.01. The int2 layers carry the largest losses, e.g. 14.down rht_gptq_int2 KL 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065] and 18.gate rht_gptq_int2 KL-minus-floor 0.00497 [Eb1dd74cd6447]. Weaker damping lets the Hessian correction act more strongly on those layers. Comparing this grid with the act_order-only grid isolates the effect of damping.
